message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of J.K. Rowling’s most popular books:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also known as *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | The first book in the Harry Potter series; introduces the wizarding world. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment; follows Harry’s return to Hogwarts. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Triwizard Tournament. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on the rise of Voldemort and the formation of Dumbledore’s Army. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince** | 2005 | Sixth book; delves into Voldemort’s past and the Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Seventh and final book; concludes the epic saga. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel; a political drama set in a small English town. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable about a mythical beast, released as a free e‑book during the pandemic. |
| **Cormoran Strike Series** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013–present | A detective thriller series featuring private investigator Cormoran Strike and his assistant Robin Ellacott. |

These titles have garnered massive readerships worldwide and have been adapted into blockbuster films (the Harry Potter movies) and stage productions. If you’re looking for more details or recommendations based on your interests, feel free to ask!
